command.mac:
cd ~
claude 'Check two things on this Mac and give PASS or FAIL for each, with the lines you read. Change nothing. 1. Decision watch: read the last 20 lines of ~/.claude/decision-watch-shadow/shadow.log. PASS if the newest END line names a verdict such as ALLOW or FLAG. FAIL if it says UNKNOWN or the file is missing. 2. Mods: run claude plugin list. PASS if the decision watch mod shows 0.0.11 or later and each claude-settings mod shows the version on main of github.com/shivinate7/claude-settings.'
command.powershell:
cd $env:USERPROFILE
claude 'Check two things on this PC and give PASS or FAIL for each, with the lines you read. Change nothing. 1. Decision watch: read the last 20 lines of .claude\decision-watch-shadow\shadow.log in my home folder. PASS if the newest END line names a verdict such as ALLOW or FLAG. FAIL if it says UNKNOWN or the file is missing. 2. Mods: run claude plugin list. PASS if the decision watch mod shows 0.0.11 or later and each claude-settings mod shows the version on main of github.com/shivinate7/claude-settings.'

context:
Both already passed on your Mac on Oct 27. Each step (c29 and c58) can only close when Windows passes too.

The decision watch (c29) is a small program that reads each turn and records whether it followed your recorded decisions; "judged" means it ran and gave a verdict, "UNKNOWN" means it could not run. The mods (c58) are the small add-ons claude-settings installs into the Claude app; each should update itself to the version on main.
